fullAnalysis: At first glance, do not suggest one clean pattern. The board only tightens once a later clue makes the shared category feel much more specific. That is why guesses like "Tourist attractions" and "Popular vacation destinations" can feel plausible at the start. The clue that changes the frame is "the key clue".

From there, reading them as one clean category explains the board more cleanly than broader labels. Once that frame clicks, names like stop feeling miscellaneous and start looking like members of one shelf. The clues are all well-known, but they could be associated with other locations if taken individually.

lessons.title: Broad clues can create the wrong frame early
lessons.body: When the first clues are very open-ended, it is often better to wait for a more specific word before locking in a category.

lessons.title: The narrowing clue matters more than the loudest clue
lessons.body: the key clue is what organizes this board. Once one clue produces a precise natural reading, re-check the earlier clues under that same frame.

lessons.title: Prefer precise category fit over broad topic logic
lessons.body: When problem-solving, consider what details are unique versus commonly shared.
